SMTO-CFG-0080 — SMTO can't resume this task's saved Skill settings

GUID: fa6b8474-3891-56f6-b2f6-cc32b00ff088
Slug: capability-selection-snapshot-missing
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_selection

What happened

  • The saved record of which Skills and tools this task may use is missing or damaged, so SMTO won't continue the task from it. It won't guess which tools to allow.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task in the conversation and read its activity to see which steps already finished. Some actions may already have happened, and repeating them could, for example, send the same email twice.
  2. Send a new message that asks only for the work that still needs doing. A new request gets fresh Skill settings, and the damaged task's record is left untouched.
  3. If you recently restored or imported SMTO data, tell the person who manages SMTO before sending more requests. Data restored from a different SMTO version can leave task records that this version can't read.

What success looks like

  • The new request starts and shows its selected capabilities in the task activity.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete or edit the old task's saved data to make it resume; they may need it to see what happened.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The run's saved capability selection authority failed integrity checks (missing authority fields, ceiling digest mismatch, Always or catalog IDs outside the ceiling, or an inconsistent selection epoch history), so it cannot be restored.

What this means

  • Saved selection authority lacks required fields, has an invalid digest/ceiling/catalog relationship, or retained selection epochs fail integrity checks. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Saved selection authority lacks required fields, has an invalid digest/ceiling/catalog relationship, or retained selection epochs fail integrity checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare authority fields, digests, allowed sets and sequential epochs while preserving original data.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run state's capability_selection_config, capability_ceiling, capability_candidate_catalog and capability_selections against validate_authority and validate_selection while preserving the original data. Restore a supported valid snapshot, or reconcile what the run already executed and submit distinct new work; never rebuild the authority fields by guesswork.
  • Preserve the affected snapshot and use supported repair or a fresh task after reconciling original work; do not reconstruct authority by guessing missing fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported valid retained snapshot is restored, or distinct new work gets newly accepted authority.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
